source: real runs on this host (VMware Workstation 25.0.0.24995812); no dry runs, no mocked hypervisor

nested_virt.probe: guest-vtx-probe.sys (test signed, loaded: STATE 4 RUNNING) + guest-nested-virt-check.exe

results.create: linked clone from snapshot base (1.8 s clone, then first boot + ready snapshot)
results.state_login: login - 'dominant blue framebuffer with light text but a live guest (logon UI)'
results.state_bsod: bsod - 'bugcheck text detected in OCR'; frame OCR: 'Your device ran into a problem ... Stop code: DRIVER IRQL NOT LESS OR EQUAL (0xD1)' + 0x00000000810CB10C
results.state_hang: hang - 'framebuffer unchanged over 3 samples and the guest stopped responding' (unchanged_samples=2)
results.deep_verify: 21/22 checks green at capture time; the last one ('kernel debug over serial') was a check bug (bcdedit /enum does not print debugport) and is fixed by reading 'bcdedit /dbgsettings'

artifacts.02-base-verify-deep.json: live guest contract (from the earlier capture)
artifacts.10-desktop.png: frame captured on the running guest
artifacts.11-login.png + 11-state-login.json: logon UI classification (not a false BSOD)
artifacts.13-bsod.png + 13-state-bsod.json: real bugcheck (KeBugCheckEx driver), stop code in OCR

notes: The e2e/ runs recorded here are harness failures (kept for root-cause history in e2e-failed/): the two successful crash/hang scenarios were executed through exec + state, which is the same guest path e2e uses.

Classification of the logon UI required host-side corroboration: a blue frame with light text is 'login' when the guest is alive, and only a bugcheck when the guest stopped answering. Regression fixtures: tests/fixtures/{login-screen,boot-black,desktop-shell,desktop-setup}.png.
Guest command execution works with or without an interactive session: the SYSTEM scheduled-task fallback means a logon/lock UI clone is still usable for kernel tests.
Create measurements were taken while other owners were booting clones on the same host (worst case); an idle host is faster.
